display.text:
# UltraPlan Go

UltraPlan Go is a local-first CLI for durable architecture studies and governed sprint delivery. It initializes study workspaces, runs source and dimension analyses through agentwrap/OpenCode, synthesizes reports, validates artifacts, executes sprint plans, runs resumable automated reviews, drives review-gated smoke verification, and embeds manually invoked skills for every sprint stage.

This release includes study workflows and the grounded governed sprint chain `requirements -> code-context -> sprint-index -> technical-handbook -> area-reasoning -> reasoning -> plan -> execute -> review -> smoke`, including integrated `sprint verify`, durable review resume, focused review reruns, explicit diagnostic smoke overrides, and opt-in Git publication after completed stages. `code-context.md` stores repository-relative references only; later agent-backed stages receive one byte-stable shared prefix containing the exact requirements and context-pack bytes plus bounded transient live source evidence. Agents may still inspect additional repository files. Issue management, hosted SaaS, multi-user collaboration, general Git automation beyond stage publication and sprint worktree creation, retrieval/indexing, UltraPlan cache ownership, signing, notarization, tags, and artifact upload remain deferred.

Phase 3 operators should start with the [CLI reference](docs/cli-reference.md), [recovery runbook](docs/recovery.md), [JSON schema contract](docs/phase3-json-schemas.md), and [legacy verification migration guide](docs/phase3-migration.md). The authoritative product requirements, technical requirements, architecture, roadmap, and sprint plans live in the adjacent `ultraplan-go-workspace/projects/ultraplan-go/` planning workspace; this repository does not duplicate them.

## Install

Install to your user bin directory, which keeps the `ultraplan` command in the same place for future upgrades:

```bash
./scripts/install-ultraplan.sh
```

That script installs `ultraplan` from the current checkout to `~/.local/bin` by default. It can be run from any directory. If you prefer a different bin directory, set `GOBIN` first:

```bash
GOBIN="$HOME/bin" ./scripts/install-ultraplan.sh
```

Build from source:

```bash
go build -o bin/ultraplan ./cmd/ultraplan
```

Run the built binary:

```bash
./bin/ultraplan --help
```

For local release artifacts, see [docs/release-checklist.md](docs/release-checklist.md). This repository packages Linux and macOS binaries under `dist/` when the release checklist is run.

## Quick Start

Initialize a workspace:

```bash
ultraplan init-workspace --path .
```

Check workspace, config, and runtime health:

```bash
ultraplan health
```

Inspect effective configuration:

```bash
ultraplan config show
ultraplan config show --json
```

Initialize a study from YAML:

```bash
ultraplan study init study-init.yml --no-clone
```

List studies, sources, and dimensions:

```bash
ultraplan study list
ultraplan study <study> list
```

Preview prompts without runtime execution:

```bash
ultraplan study <study> prompt analysis 01 <source>
ultraplan study <study> prompt synthesis 01 --output previews/synthesis-01.txt
```

Install editable copies of the built-in prompts and templates only when you want to customize them:

```bash
ultraplan defaults install --dry-run
ultraplan defaults install
```

Materialise all manually invoked stage skills, or just one:

```bash
ultraplan skills materialise
ultraplan skills materialise reasoning
ultraplan skills materialise code-context
```

Run study work:

```bash
ultraplan study <study> run 01 <source>
ultraplan study <study> synthesize 01
ultraplan study <study> run-all --parallel 3
ultraplan study <study> run-loop --parallel 3
ultraplan study <study> run-loop --dimension 01 --source <source> --parallel 1
```

`run-loop` resumes shared study progress by default. Dimension/source filters advance only that slice of the study graph while progress is still stored in `studies/<study>/.ultraplan/run-state.json`. Use `--reset` only when you intentionally want to archive and rebuild study progress.

Validate, inspect status, summarize, and extract code references:

```bash
ultraplan study <study> validate --json
ultraplan study <study> status
ultraplan study <study> summary
ultraplan code studies/<study>/reports/final/01-topic.md --json
```

Inspect planning projects and validate governed sprint artifacts:

```bash
ultraplan project list
ultraplan project <project> status
ultraplan project <project> validate
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> status
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> validate requirements
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> validate sprint-index
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> validate execute
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> flow --to requirements --dry-run
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> flow --to plan --dry-run
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> flow --to execute --dry-run
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> execute --resume
```

## Documentation

- [User guide](docs/user-guide.md): end-to-end study workflow.
- [CLI reference](docs/cli-reference.md): public commands, flags, exit classes, and stable JSON surfaces.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): `ultraplan.yml`, environment overrides, precedence, redaction, and runtime mapping.
- [Stage skills](docs/stage-skills.md): manual invocation, prerequisite interaction, materialisation, and state ownership.
- [Recovery runbook](docs/recovery.md): validation failures, stale locks, cancellation, partial runs, and safe retry.
- [OpenCode smoke](docs/opencode-smoke.md): gated real-runtime smoke procedure outside default tests.
- [Planning smoke](docs/planning-smoke.md): gated planning flow smoke procedure.
- [Migration from `.ultra/cli`](docs/migration-from-ultra-cli.md): planning artifact migration notes.
- [Release checklist](docs/release-checklist.md): local release gates, packaging, checksums, and security review.

## Workspace Model

`init-workspace` creates the minimal required workspace:

```text
README.md
ultraplan.yml
studies/
```

Prompts and templates are built into the CLI. A workspace does not need `prompts/` or `templates/` to run. If a workspace file exists at the same relative path, it overrides the built-in default. Use `ultraplan defaults install` to materialize editable copies:

```text
prompts/
  base.md
  synthesize.md
  create-sprint-index.md
  create-technical-handbook.md
  create-area-reasoning.md
  create-sprint-reasoning.md
  plan-sprint.md
  ...
templates/
  repo-analysis.md
  report.md
  sprint-index.md
  technical-handbook.md
  sprint-reasoning.md
  sprint-plan.md
  ...
```

If an existing workspace prompt or template differs from the built-in default, `defaults install` lists the customized file and asks before overwriting it. Use `--force` only when you intentionally want to replace customized files without confirmation.

Reasoning defaults may also be specialised per project. UltraPlan resolves
`create-area-reasoning.md`, `create-sprint-reasoning.md`, and
`sprint-reasoning.md` in this order: project override, workspace override,
then built-in default. Project overrides live at:

```text
projects/<project>/prompts/create-area-reasoning.md
projects/<project>/prompts/create-sprint-reasoning.md
projects/<project>/templates/sprint-reasoning.md
```

Studies live under `studies/<study>/` with editable source, dimension, report, run-state, and summary artifacts. Directory sources are analyzed by path. Live directory-source metadata is stored in `sources/<source>.ultraplan-source.yml` or `sources/<source>/.ultraplan-source.yml`; `applicable_dimensions` there limits which dimensions apply. Top-level Markdown sources can declare the same filter in frontmatter. `study-init.yml` is retained as initialization provenance, not the live applicability contract.

Each initialized study also has an editable `studies/<study>/study.json`. Its optional `dimension_order` list runs the referenced dimensions first, in order, before the remaining dimensions. Each listed dimension completes its applicable analyses and synthesis before the next tier starts; unlisted dimensions retain natural ordering and bounded parallelism. Existing studies without `study.json` retain their current behavior.

Study reports are dimension-scoped. Per-source reports are written to `studies/<study>/reports/source/<dimension-ref>/<source>.md`, and synthesis writes `studies/<study>/reports/final/<dimension-ref>.md`.

Projects live under `projects/<project>/` with `docs/`, `roadmap.md`, `project-index.md`, and `sprints/<sprint>/`. A project can keep specialised area reasoning documents under `projects/<project>/reasoning/` and list them in `project-index.md`. Planning sprints are editable Markdown/JSON artifact chains through `requirements.md`, reference-only `code-context.md`, `sprint-index.md`, `technical-handbook.md`, optional `reasoning/*.md`, `reasoning.md`, `plan.md`, and `flow-state.json`. `flow --to plan` runs code-context exactly once after requirements.

Manually invoked stage skills are materialised under `.agents/skills/`. Each
skill contains the corresponding canonical prompt plus interactive
prerequisite, proposal, validation, and reconciliation rules. They are marked
manual-only and therefore require explicit `$ultraplan-<stage>` invocation.
`$ultraplan-code-context` is the narrow canonical-delegation exception: it invokes `ultraplan sprint "$PROJECT" "$SPRINT" flow --to code-context`, leaving target resolution, read-only runtime policy, validation, atomic promotion, and state transitions in the product operation.

## Runtime Boundary

UltraPlan owns study behavior and artifact validation. Runtime execution is delegated through `github.com/Antonio7098/agentwrap` and its OpenCode adapter. UltraPlan does not claim direct OpenCode process supervision, provider billing ownership, or provider-agnostic guarantees that bypass the configured runtime.

Default tests are offline and fake-first. Real OpenCode smoke is gated by local OpenCode, provider configuration, network availability, and a prepared workspace.

## Development

Run the offline test suite:

```bash
go test ./...
```

Run the race suite:

```bash
go test -race ./...
```

Build the CLI:

```bash
go build ./cmd/ultraplan
```

The architecture keeps product behavior inside product modules:

- `internal/workspace` owns workspace discovery, path safety, workspace validation, and embedded stage-skill materialisation.
- `internal/study` owns study workflows, prompts, validation, execution, summaries, and durable state.
- `internal/project` owns project discovery, project-index catalog validation, and project status.
- `internal/sprint` owns planning artifacts, flow state, stage validation, prompt previews, and flow execution through `plan.md`.
- `internal/codeextract` owns citation parsing and snippet extraction.
- `internal/platform/*` owns cross-cutting infrastructure and generic runtime integration.
- `internal/app` owns CLI wiring and process exit behavior.

Good overview. Now let me launch review-worker subagents for bounded discovery. My job: map execution lifecycles from request through runtime/process/cancellation/result/persistence/observation.

Candidate execution-path surfaces to discover:

1. **study-run-execution**: `study <s> run <dim> <source>` — prompt assembly → runtime session → output capture → report persistence → run-state update. Files: internal/study/run.go, prompts.go, reports.go, service.go, internal/platform/runtime/*, internal/app/run_commands.go, study_usecases.go.

2. **study-runloop-parallel-resume**: run-all/run-loop scheduling, parallelism bounds, dimension_order tiers, filters, --reset archive, run-state.json persistence/resume. Files: run_all.go, run_loop.go, run_state*.go, state_database.go, locks.go.

3. **study-synthesize-summary**: synthesize 01 → final report; status/summary observation path. Maybe fold into observation surface.

4. **sprint-flow-stage-execution**: `flow --to X` chain requirements→code-context→sprint-index→handbook→reasoning→plan: validation gates, prompt bundle build, agentwrap invocation, atomic promotion (store_fs), flow-state.json transitions. Files: internal/sprint/flow.go, artifacts.go, store_fs.go, state.go, code_context.go, context_pack.go, handbook.go, index.go, reasoning.go, plan.go, prompt_bundle.go.

5. **sprint-execute-resume-cancellation**: execute --resume loop over plan tasks, per-task state, locks, cancellation/interruption, cleanup_uncertain. Files: execute*.go, locks.go, session_state.go, verification_lock.go.

6. **review-smoke-gate**: sprint execute includes review + smoke stages; durable review resume, focused reruns, qa_*, smoke_* files, verify.go, verification_phase.go.

7. **runtime-process-supervision**: platform/runtime (opencode.go, agentwrap adapter, store.go SQLite, events.go, health.go, policy.go, opencode_maintenance.go) and platform/process (spawn, kill, pgid). Cancellation propagation.

8. **publication-and-worktrees**: gitpublish publisher, sprint publication.go, study publication.go, worktree creation for execute_target.

9. **observation surfaces data path**: status/summary/json outputs, web serve, TUI — how they read persisted state while runs are active. Bounded: app/status_json.go, study summary.go, web_usecases.go, tui_commands.go, serve_commands.go.

10. **run-control / durable operations**: internal/app/run_control.go, durable_operations.go, operation_runner.go — cross-cutting operation journaling? Also internal/runcontrol package! I haven't listed it. Let me check that too.

Also internal/productstate, internal/project, internal/workspace scaffold, internal/codeextract (code-context citation extraction is part of flow). And `internal/tui`.

I should delegate ~6-8 bounded review-worker tasks in parallel, each mapping one candidate surface's lifecycle with specific questions about entrypoints, state authorities, dependencies, outputs, failure semantics, seams. Then reconcile into the final map myself.

W2: study run-all/run-loop scheduling + resume + reset + locks + run-state persistence; also synthesize.
W3: sprint flow stage chain (`flow --to ...`) — validation gates, prompt bundle, atomic promotion, flow-state.json transitions, code-context/context-pack/codeextract involvement.
W4: sprint execute --resume loop — plan task execution, per-task state, session state, locks, cancellation/interruption handling, cleanup_uncertain.
W5: review + smoke verification gates — qa_*, smoke_*, verify.go, verification_phase/lock, focused reruns, durable review resume, diagnostic overrides.
W6: platform/runtime + platform/process — agentwrap adapter, OpenCode process spawn/supervision, events, sqlite store, health/maintenance, policy, cancellation propagation, timeouts.
W7: publication & worktrees — gitpublish publisher, sprint/study publication, worktree creation in execute_target, git_publication.go app wiring.
W8: observation/live surfaces — web server (SSE, operations, run handlers), TUI, status/summary JSON, how they observe active runs; internal/runcontrol lifecycle/process/metrics as shared operation-control substrate; app run_control.go/durable_operations.go/operation_runner.go.

That's 8 workers. That might be a lot but "use aggressively" is instructed. Each is bounded. Let me write precise prompts. All read-only research; no code changes.

Also each worker should note seams to other candidate surfaces.

Let me launch all 8 in parallel.

# Surface map: `study run-all` / `run-loop` / `synthesize` (read-only discovery, no findings)

All paths relative to `/home/antonioborgerees/coding/ultraplan/ultraplan-go`. Line numbers from current frozen tree.

---

## 1. Entrypoints

**CLI dispatch** — `internal/app/study_commands.go`
- Router: `runStudy` switch at :48-55 → `args[1] == "run-loop"` → `runStudyRunLoop(:197)`, `"run-all"` → `runStudyRunAll(:546)`, `"synthesize"` → `runStudySynthesize(:831)`; single-run at :52-53 (`runStudyRun(:802)`).
- `runStudyRunLoop` (:197): parses flags via `parseRunLoopArgs(:241)` (wraps `parseRunAllArgs(:579)`, adds `--force-unlock/--continue/--reset/--yes`), confirms destructive reset via `confirmRunLoopReplacement(:277)` ("Existing study progress is present and would be archived/replaced."), opens a durable operation (`beginDurableCLICommand(deps, OperationRequest{Kind: OperationStudyResume, ...})` :211), then calls `service.RunLoop(durable.Context(), study.RunLoopRequest{...})` (:220). Exit classification: `classifyRunAllResult(study.RunAllResult{Status: result.Status})` (:238); lock errors map to `ExitPartial` in `mapStudyRunLoopError(:354)`.
- `runStudyRunAll` (:546): `OperationStudyStart` (:555), `service.RunAll(durable.Context(), ...)` (:563).
- `runStudySynthesize` (:831): requires exactly one positional `<dimension>` (:840), `OperationStudyStart`, calls `service.Synthesize(...)` (:851).
- Service construction: `runLoopService(:318)` / `runAllService(:675)` / `executionService(:860)` — parallelism default `effective.Config.Execution.DefaultParallel` overridden by `--parallel`; wraps runtime with `controlledRuntimeFor` and publisher via `study.NewService(root.Path, study.WithRuntime(controlled, req), study.WithPublisher(stagePublisher(...)))`.
- Progress renderers: `renderRunLoopProgress(:397)` (stdout `[run-loop] ...` lines incl. throttle/restore lines), `renderRunAllRuntimeProgress(:523)` (mutex-serialized stderr `[runtime] ...`).

**Domain layer** — `internal/study`
- `Service.RunAll` — `internal/study/run_all.go:16`
- `Service.RunLoop` — `internal/study/run_loop.go:23` (doc comment :16-22: "intentionally resumable rather than exactly-once… one per-study mutator lock, atomic transition persistence, completed artifact revalidation before trust")
- `Service.RunAnalysis` — `internal/study/run.go:19`; `Service.Synthesize` — `internal/study/synthesize.go:8`
- `Service.RunLoopDiagnostics` infra — `internal/study/run_loop_diagnostics.go:91-244` (`newRunLoopDiagnostics`, `start`, `sample`, `scheduling`, `storage`)
- Web/TUI operation path also enters here: `internal/app/operation_runner.go:131-151` runs the same `service.RunLoop` for `OperationStudyStart/OperationStudyResume`; cancel op at :152-162 calls `study.CancelRunLoop`.

---

## 2. Work-graph construction

- Enumeration: `ListStudy` (`internal/study/service.go:118-146`) → `DiscoverSources`, `DiscoverDimensions`, `LoadStudyConfig` (dimension_order from `studies/<s>/study.json`, `internal/study/config.go:37-81`; duplicates/unknown refs rejected as `ErrStudyConfigInvalid`).
- **Run-all path**: filters via `resolveDimensions`/`resolveSources` (`run_all.go:162-190`) then `buildAnalysisTasks(dimensions, sources)` (`run_all.go:192-203`) = cross-product filtered by `SourceAppliesToDimension` (`prompts.go:163`; applicability rules in `applicability.go:3-17` `GetApplicableSources`). Tiering: `dimensionExecutionGroups(selected, priority)` (`run_all.go:118-143`) — each `dimension_order` entry becomes its own group (barrier: analyses + synthesis of that dimension complete before next group), remaining dimensions form one final natural-order group.
- **Run-loop path**: full graph built/persisted by `NewRunState` → `buildCurrentTaskGraph` (`run_state.go:102-174`): per dimension, one analysis task per applicable source plus a synthesis task whose `Dependencies` list the analysis task IDs; tasks sorted by ID; an `ApplicabilityFingerprint` sha256 over dimension/source tuples is stored (:172-173). Dimensions/sources sorted by Number/Name for determinism (`run_state.go:36-50`). Task IDs: `analysisTaskID` / `synthesisTaskID` (`run_state.go:447-460`).
- **Filter slicing in run-loop**: scope is computed, not graph-destructive — `runLoopScope` (`run_loop.go:650-666`): analysis IDs in scope per applicable source; synthesis included only when "…`!sourceFiltered || len(applicable) == len(allApplicable)`" (a partial-source filter excludes that dimension's synthesis). Scope is used by `filterRunState` (:668-684), counts (`summarizeRunStateCountsForScope` :518), scheduling (`runnableTaskIDs(state, scope, …)`), while the persisted state remains the shared full-study graph.

---

## 3. Parallelism mechanism

- **RunAll**: fixed-size worker pool — `taskCh := make(chan int)` + `req.Parallelism` goroutines (`run_all.go:56-90`); producer feeds indices unless `ctx.Err() != nil` (pending/cancelled placeholder results). Synthesis phase is serial after `wg.Wait()` (:92-114).
- **RunLoop**: scheduler loop + unbuffered handoff — claims up to `available := effectiveParallelism - active` runnable task IDs, spawns `go runTask(id)` per claim, then blocks on `<-done` to refill one slot ("Each task owns its OpenCode database, so a completed slot can be refilled without waiting for sibling cleanup." `run_loop.go:435-438`). Started events are emitted at claim time so ordering matches scheduler tier order (:424-428 comment).
- **Dynamic throttling** each iteration:
  - Memory: `readMemoryPressure()` (`memory_pressure.go:18-49`, thresholds 15%/25% of MemTotal) decrements/restores `effectiveParallelism` under `mu` (`run_loop.go:348-374`), emitting `parallelism.throttled`/`restored` diagnostics + progress events.
  - Disk: `readSchedulerDiskPressure` (`disk_pressure.go:38-52`; pressured <1536 MiB free or ≥90%, critical <768 MiB or ≥97%); admission pause with aggressive store cleanup when no workers active (`run_loop.go:375-401`, waits 30 s when idle+pressured); hard cap via `diskParallelismCap` (`disk_pressure.go:21-36`, 512 MiB budget per worker).
- **Shared mutable state**: `state RunState` guarded by `mu sync.Mutex` (`run_loop.go:100`); all mutations through `update(id, fn)` (:187-199) which bumps `stateVersion` and triggers debounced persist; `saveMu` serializes disk writes (:149); `historyMu` guards ledger appends (:209); `errMu` guards `firstErr` (:230-246). Progress emission is mutex-guarded (:117-148). Per-task isolation of agent state comes from `req.RuntimeStorePath = runtimepkg.ScopedRuntimeStorePath(...)` keyed by owner string (`run.go:122-127`, `platform/runtime/store.go:48-51` → hash-of-owner `opencode.db` per task).
- Cap sanity: operations layer enforces 1..64 (`operations.go:306-308`).

---

## 4. Durable progress authority

- Files (under `studies/<study>/.ultraplan/`, `domain.go:4-6`): `run-state.json` (`RunStatePath`, `run_state.go:188-190`), `runs/tasks.jsonl` ledger (`run_history.go:68-70`), `runs/summary.md` (:72-74), `run-loop.lock` (`locks.go:25-27`), `diagnostics/run-loop-memory.jsonl` (`run_loop_diagnostics.go:93`), `archive/run-state-<ts>.json` (`run_loop.go:559-573`).
- Schema: `RunState{schema_version, run_id, filters, config_summary, applicability_fingerprint, tasks[], complete}` (`run_state_domain.go:19-30`); `TaskState` includes `Attempts, RetryAfter, LastError, Validation, Agent metadata, Session checkpoint, Dependencies` (:47-80). `ValidateRunState` (`state.go:121-166`) enforces schema version 1, unique task IDs, valid statuses, valid session checkpoints.
- **Dual authority**: `LoadRunState` prefers the productstate DB when present (`state.go:27-35` → `loadRunStateDatabase`, `state_database.go:17-41`: header JSON + one item per task, kind `study_run`, scope = study name). `SaveRunState` (`state.go:59-71`): if DB authoritative, save there and — "if !state.Complete { return nil }" — only also write the JSON file when the whole study is complete. `MigrateRunStateToDatabase` exists (`state_database.go:78-80`).
- **Write mechanics**: temp-file + fsync + rename + dir sync (`saveRunStateWithHooks`, `state.go:73-119`); history appends rewrite-whole-file atomically with trailing-partial-line repair (`atomicWriteRunHistory`, `trimInvalidTrailingRunHistory`, `run_history.go:104-148`).
- **Ordering vs artifacts**: inside `runTask` (`run_loop.go:293-339`): claim transition (`running`, Attempts++, session cleared) is persisted *before* the runtime call; during execution, `checkpointSession` persists the session checkpoint on every session event (:307-313, wired via `OnSession`→`req.OnEvent` checkpoint in `run.go:149-164`); artifact write happens inside the runtime call; validation occurs inside `RunAnalysis`/`Synthesize` (`run.go:94-96`, `synthesize.go:91-93`); only then does `applyExecutionResult` persist the terminal transition, followed by `recordHistory` (:334-335). So: artifact → validate → state-write → history-append.
- **Crash between artifact-write and state-write**: task still says `running` → on restart `ResumeValidateRunState` resets running/validating/waiting/cancelled → pending (`run_state.go:290-301`) and re-validates any `completed` task's artifact, demoting it to failed if invalid (:312-350). `RestoreCompletedRunHistory` (`run_state.go:366-429`) can re-promote reopened tasks to completed *only* if a passed-validation history record exists — "A history record is required, so arbitrary stale files are never adopted" (:365).
- Debounced persistence: `persist(taskID, force)` coalesces by version, min 250 ms between non-forced saves, clone-under-lock before write (`run_loop.go:153-185`); final forced `save()` + `SyncRunHistory` after loop exit (:458-464).

## 5. Resume semantics & --reset archive flow

- Startup sequence in `RunLoop`: acquire per-study lock → load-or-create state (`loadOrCreateRunLoopState`, `run_loop.go:536-557`) → startup runtime-store cleanup (`CleanupRuntimeStores(…72h, 2 GiB…)` :60-61) → `ReconcileRunState` (graph diff, reopen synthesis whose deps changed :86-92) → `ResumeValidateRunState` (revalidate completed artifacts; reset active states) → optional `RestoreCompletedRunHistory` (skipped entirely when `req.Reset`) → initial `SaveRunState` + `SyncRunHistory` (:69-82).
- Completed-work detection on restart: status `completed` survives reconciliation only if `ValidateSourceReport`/`ValidateFinalReport` still pass (`run_state.go:312-350`); test pins rerun-after-artifact-deletion (`run_loop_test.go:257-278`). Failed tasks with future `RetryAfter` become `retrying`; expired ones go pending (:303-311).
- Resume across processes keeps session checkpoints: cancelled tasks retain `Session`; next invocation resumes with `SessionAction: "continue"` and falls back to fresh on incompatible fingerprint (`run.go:139-179`, `studySessionCompatible` :251-253). Pinned by `TestRunLoopPersistsAndContinuesCancelledStudySession` (`run_loop_test.go:132-181`).
- `--reset` flow: CLI confirm (`confirmRunLoopReplacement`) → `loadOrCreateRunLoopState` sees `req.Reset`, skips load, calls `archiveRunStateIfExists` (`run_loop.go:559-573`): renames `run-state.json` to `.ultraplan/archive/run-state-<UTC-timestamp>.json`, then builds fresh state. Only the state file is archived; ledger/history is preserved and keys prevent duplicate records (`recordHistory` dedup via `historyKeys`). Pinned by `TestRunLoopDefaultResumesExistingStateAndResetStartsFresh` (`run_loop_test.go:280-331`, asserts archive entries exist) and CLI `TestStudyRunLoopCommandConfirmsBeforeReplacingExistingState`.

## 6. Synthesize step

- Within `RunAll`: after each dimension-execution group's analyses complete, serially per dimension (`run_all.go:92-114`); skipped if no analyses ran (`hasAnalysisForDimension`) or blocked by `synthesisBlockers` (any non-completed sibling → `preflight_blocked` with blocker paths, :213-224). `Synthesize` itself re-runs preflight validation of every applicable source report and returns `preflight_blocked` before any runtime call (`synthesize.go:31-42`).
- Within `RunLoop`: synthesis tasks are graph nodes depending on their analyses; scheduler admits them once deps complete (`runnableTaskIDs` :613-631 checks `dependenciesCompleteFrom`); if dependencies reach terminal-but-not-complete states, `markSynthesisDependenciesFailed` fails the synthesis with code `synthesis.dependencies_failed` (:280-285, :857-865). Dimension order is "priority, but not a barrier" (:611-612 comment) so synthesis starts as soon as its own deps finish (`TestRunLoopSynthesizesDimensionAsSoonAsItsAnalysisCompletes`).
- Manual: `study synthesize <dim>` command (§1). Final report path: `FinalReportPath` (`reports.go:12`); publication deferred in loop mode (`DeferPublication: true`, `run_loop.go:316/:323`) and executed by a dedicated publication goroutine draining `publicationJobs` (:247-262) plus end-of-run `publishRunLoopState` publishing state+ledger+summary together (`publication.go:45-63`).

## 7. Cancellation / interruption

- Signals: `cmd/ultraplan/main.go:19` `signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)` → `deps.ctx` → `beginDurableCLICommand` derives the cancellable operation context (`durable_operations.go:130`); run-control's watchdog also cancels on `CancellationRequested` or lost heartbeat/snapshot errors (`controlOperation`, `durable_operations.go:223-264`).
- RunAll on cancel: producer stops dispatching, workers mark remaining tasks cancelled placeholders; synthesis emits `cancelled` results; `statusRunAll(result, ctx.Err() != nil)` → `cancelled` (`run_all.go:49`, :243-245).
- RunLoop on cancel: outer loop condition drains active workers then exits (`run_loop.go:344`); claimed-but-unstarted `runTask` marks its own task cancelled via `markTaskCancelled` (:264-270); in-flight tasks get `cancelled` category from runtime (`statusForRuntimeFailure`, `run.go:310-315`); unscheduled tasks stay `pending` (pinned by `TestRunLoopCancellationDoesNotCancelUnscheduledTasks`, which asserts zero history records too).
- Locking: `AcquireRunLoopLock` uses `O_EXCL` create, PID liveness check (`processAlive`, `locks.go:17-23`) with stale-lock removal-and-retry (:61-86), redacted command capture (`sanitizeCommand` :184-202); ownership-checked release refusing foreign locks (:116-118). `CancelRunLoop` SIGINTs the live owner cross-process (:141-159); `ForceUnlockRunLoop` removes the file (:161-167). Observation-side `RunLoopActive` treats missing/malformed/stale locks as inactive (:131-137).
- `cleanup_uncertain.go` role: server-shutdown path writes `cleanup-uncertain.json` *without* taking the lock ("the original owner may still hold that lock", :28-30); `ReconcileInterruptedRun` (:66-90) later takes the lock and converts orphaned active states into explicit `workflow.interrupted` cancellations (`reconcileInterruptedRunLocked` :100-150) — this is the serve/web shutdown complement; the CLI `RunLoop` instead relies on `ResumeValidateRunState` resetting actives to pending.

## 8. Failure isolation

- RunAll: a failing analysis becomes `failedAnalysisResult` and the pool continues (`run_all.go:75-78`); synthesis then reports blockers. No retries at this layer.
- RunLoop: runtime failures do **not** stop scheduling — they're folded into task state by `applyExecutionResult` (`run_loop.go:779-826`): retryable categories (`rate_limit, timeout, provider_unavailable, runtime_unavailable` → `executionShouldRetry` :841-848) set `TaskStatusRetrying` with `RetryAfter` (+10 min rate-limit, else +2 min, :850-855); others → `failed`. Scheduler waits via `waitUntilRetry` emitting retry-wait progress (:441-448, :481-501). What *does* stop new scheduling is `firstErr` — persistence/history/publication machinery errors (`stopScheduling`, :345-347) — while already-active workers drain. Sibling failure → synthesis marked failed only when deps are terminal-non-complete (`markSynthesisDependenciesFailed`), pinned by `TestRunLoopMarksSynthesisFailedWhenDependenciesTerminal`.

## 9. Observation

- `study status [--json]`: loads state, reconciles in memory only, attaches `LockInfoForStatus`, renders counts/Active/Failed sections (`study_commands.go:1112-1210`).
- Live progress: `renderRunLoopProgress` stdout lines with scope-vs-study counters; runtime events summarized with redaction (`runtimeProgressSummary` :429, `config.RedactValue("runtime."+key,…)`).
- Diagnostics: JSONL sampler at `diagnostics/run-loop-memory.jsonl` (5 s ticker, 8 MB rotate, phases `state.save.end`, `runtime.start/end`, `parallelism.throttled`, `disk.admission_paused`, child RSS/CPU per task); read back by `LoadRunLoopResourceHistory` (:422-454) and `SummarizeParallelismThrottle` (:401-420).
- History aggregation: append-only `tasks.jsonl` with idempotent key `RunID|TaskID|Attempts|CompletedAtRFC3339Nano` (`run_history.go:306-312`), crash-tolerant tail handling (:262-270 comment: "A crash or full disk can leave only the final JSONL record partial"); `runs summary` subcommand refreshes `summary.md` without runtime (`app/study_runs_commands.go:16-33`); `RenderRunHistorySummary` produces status/remaining/dimension/source/runtime/recent/slowest/failed tables (`run_history_summary.go:25-57`).

## 10. Pinning tests

`internal/study/run_all_test.go`
- `TestRunAllFiltersMatrixSynthesisSummary(:56)` — filter matrix, 3 runtime calls, summary written
- `TestRunAllPreflightFailuresStartNoRuntime(:82)` — bad refs / parallelism=0 start no runtime
- `TestRunAllEmptyApplicableMatrixSkipsSynthesisAndRuntime(:101)` — empty applicability ⇒ zero calls, exact CSV

- `TestRunAllCompletesConfiguredPriorityDimensionsBeforeRemainingDimensions(:155)` — strict group barrier order with `dimension_order:["02"]`

`internal/study/run_loop_test.go`
- `TestRunLoopRefillsAWorkerSlotWithoutWaitingForTheBatch(:57)` — continuous refill + unique per-task runtime stores
- `TestRunLoopPersistsAndContinuesCancelledStudySession(:132)` — session checkpoint survive/resume/continue
- `TestRunLoopCreatesDurableStateRunsTasksAndReleasesLock(:183)` — durable state contents, lock released
- `TestRunLoopProgressUsesCountOnlySummaries(:225)` — progress carries counts, not task payloads
- `TestRunLoopContinueResumesAndRevalidatesCompletedStateBeforeScheduling(:257)` — deleted completed report gets rerun
- `TestRunLoopDefaultResumesExistingStateAndResetStartsFresh(:280)` — shared-state resume; reset archives + rebuilds
- `TestRunLoopSynthesizesDimensionAsSoonAsItsAnalysisCompletes(:333)`; `TestRunLoopStartsPriorityTierBeforeLaterTiers(:364)`
- `TestRunLoopCancellationDoesNotCancelUnscheduledTasks(:395)`; `TestRunLoopMarksSynthesisFailedWhenDependenciesTerminal(:427)`

`internal/study/run_loop_diagnostics_test.go`

`internal/app`

## 11. Seams

- **Single run** (`study run`/`synthesize`): same `RunAnalysis`/`Synthesize` service methods, immediate publication (`DeferPublication` false), no lock/state/ledger — `executionService` (`study_commands.go:860-878`).

- `Service.RunLoop` — `internal/study/run_loop.go:23` (doc comment :16-22: "intentionally resumable rather than exactly-once… one per-study mutator lock, atomic transition persistence, completed artifact revalidation before trust")

## 2. Work-graph construction

- Enumeration: `ListStudy` (`internal/study/service.go:118-146`) → `DiscoverSources`, `DiscoverDimensions`, `LoadStudyConfig` (dimension_order from `studies/<s>/study.json`, `internal/study/config.go:37-81`; duplicates/unknown refs rejected as `ErrStudyConfigInvalid`).
- **Run-all path**: filters via `resolveDimensions`/`resolveSources` (`run_all.go:162-190`) then `buildAnalysisTasks(dimensions, sources)` (`run_all.go:192-203`) = cross-product filtered by `SourceAppliesToDimension` (`prompts.go:163`; applicability rules in `applicability.go:3-17` `GetApplicableSources`). Tiering: `dimensionExecutionGroups(selected, priority)` (`run_all.go:118-143`) — each `dimension_order` entry becomes its own group (barrier: analyses + synthesis of that dimension complete before next group), remaining dimensions form one final natural-order group.
- **Run-loop path**: full graph built/persisted by `NewRunState` → `buildCurrentTaskGraph` (`run_state.go:102-174`): per dimension, one analysis task per applicable source plus a synthesis task whose `Dependencies` list the analysis task IDs; tasks sorted by ID; an `ApplicabilityFingerprint` sha256 over dimension/source tuples is stored (:172-173). Dimensions/sources sorted by Number/Name for determinism (`run_state.go:36-50`). Task IDs: `analysisTaskID` / `synthesisTaskID` (`run_state.go:447-460`).
- **Filter slicing in run-loop**: scope is computed, not graph-destructive — `runLoopScope` (`run_loop.go:650-666`): analysis IDs in scope per applicable source; synthesis included only when "…`!sourceFiltered || len(applicable) == len(allApplicable)`" (a partial-source filter excludes that dimension's synthesis). Scope is used by `filterRunState` (:668-684), counts (`summarizeRunStateCountsForScope` :518), scheduling (`runnableTaskIDs(state, scope, …)`), while the persisted state remains the shared full-study graph.

---

## 3. Parallelism mechanism

- **RunAll**: fixed-size worker pool — `taskCh := make(chan int)` + `req.Parallelism` goroutines (`run_all.go:56-90`); producer feeds indices unless `ctx.Err() != nil` (pending/cancelled placeholder results). Synthesis phase is serial after `wg.Wait()` (:92-114).
- **RunLoop**: scheduler loop + unbuffered handoff — claims up to `available := effectiveParallelism - active` runnable task IDs, spawns `go runTask(id)` per claim, then blocks on `<-done` to refill one slot ("Each task owns its OpenCode database, so a completed slot can be refilled without waiting for sibling cleanup." `run_loop.go:435-438`). Started events are emitted at claim time so ordering matches scheduler tier order (:424-428 comment).
- **Dynamic throttling** each iteration:
  - Memory: `readMemoryPressure()` (`memory_pressure.go:18-49`, thresholds 15%/25% of MemTotal) decrements/restores `effectiveParallelism` under `mu` (`run_loop.go:348-374`), emitting `parallelism.throttled`/`restored` diagnostics + progress events.
  - Disk: `readSchedulerDiskPressure` (`disk_pressure.go:38-52`; pressured <1536 MiB free or ≥90%, critical <768 MiB or ≥97%); admission pause with aggressive store cleanup when no workers active (`run_loop.go:375-401`, waits 30 s when idle+pressured); hard cap via `diskParallelismCap` (`disk_pressure.go:21-36`, 512 MiB budget per worker).
- **Shared mutable state**: `state RunState` guarded by `mu sync.Mutex` (`run_loop.go:100`); all mutations through `update(id, fn)` (:187-199) which bumps `stateVersion` and triggers debounced persist; `saveMu` serializes disk writes (:149); `historyMu` guards ledger appends (:209); `errMu` guards `firstErr` (:230-246). Progress emission is mutex-guarded (:117-148). Per-task isolation of agent state comes from `req.RuntimeStorePath = runtimepkg.ScopedRuntimeStorePath(...)` keyed by owner string (`run.go:122-127`, `platform/runtime/store.go:48-51` → hash-of-owner `opencode.db` per task).
- Cap sanity: operations layer enforces 1..64 (`operations.go:306-308`).

---

## 4. Durable progress authority

- Files (under `studies/<study>/.ultraplan/`, `domain.go:4-6`): `run-state.json` (`RunStatePath`, `run_state.go:188-190`), `runs/tasks.jsonl` ledger (`run_history.go:68-70`), `runs/summary.md` (:72-74), `run-loop.lock` (`locks.go:25-27`), `diagnostics/run-loop-memory.jsonl` (`run_loop_diagnostics.go:93`), `archive/run-state-<ts>.json` (`run_loop.go:559-573`).
- Schema: `RunState{schema_version, run_id, filters, config_summary, applicability_fingerprint, tasks[], complete}` (`run_state_domain.go:19-30`); `TaskState` includes `Attempts, RetryAfter, LastError, Validation, Agent metadata, Session checkpoint, Dependencies` (:47-80). `ValidateRunState` (`state.go:121-166`) enforces schema version 1, unique task IDs, valid statuses, valid session checkpoints.
- **Dual authority**: `LoadRunState` prefers the productstate DB when present (`state.go:27-35` → `loadRunStateDatabase`, `state_database.go:17-41`: header JSON + one item per task, kind `study_run`, scope = study name). `SaveRunState` (`state.go:59-71`): if DB authoritative, save there and — "if !state.Complete { return nil }" — only also write the JSON file when the whole study is complete. `MigrateRunStateToDatabase` exists (`state_database.go:78-80`).
- **Write mechanics**: temp-file + fsync + rename + dir sync (`saveRunStateWithHooks`, `state.go:73-119`); history appends rewrite-whole-file atomically with trailing-partial-line repair (`atomicWriteRunHistory`, `trimInvalidTrailingRunHistory`, `run_history.go:104-148`).
- **Ordering vs artifacts**: inside `runTask` (`run_loop.go:293-339`): claim transition (`running`, Attempts++, session cleared) is persisted *before* the runtime call; during execution, `checkpointSession` persists the session checkpoint on every session event (:307-313, wired via `OnSession`→`req.OnEvent` checkpoint in `run.go:149-164`); artifact write happens inside the runtime call; validation occurs inside `RunAnalysis`/`Synthesize` (`run.go:94-96`, `synthesize.go:91-93`); only then does `applyExecutionResult` persist the terminal transition, followed by `recordHistory` (:334-335). So: artifact → validate → state-write → history-append.
- **Crash between artifact-write and state-write**: task still says `running` → on restart `ResumeValidateRunState` resets running/validating/waiting/cancelled → pending (`run_state.go:290-301`) and re-validates any `completed` task's artifact, demoting it to failed if invalid (:312-350). `RestoreCompletedRunHistory` (`run_state.go:366-429`) can re-promote reopened tasks to completed *only* if a passed-validation history record exists — "A history record is required, so arbitrary stale files are never adopted" (:365).
- Debounced persistence: `persist(taskID, force)` coalesces by version, min 250 ms between non-forced saves, clone-under-lock before write (`run_loop.go:153-185`); final forced `save()` + `SyncRunHistory` after loop exit (:458-464).

## 5. Resume semantics & --reset archive flow

- Startup sequence in `RunLoop`: acquire per-study lock → load-or-create state (`loadOrCreateRunLoopState`, `run_loop.go:536-557`) → startup runtime-store cleanup (`CleanupRuntimeStores(…72h, 2 GiB…)` :60-61) → `ReconcileRunState` (graph diff, reopen synthesis whose deps changed :86-92) → `ResumeValidateRunState` (revalidate completed artifacts; reset active states) → optional `RestoreCompletedRunHistory` (skipped entirely when `req.Reset`) → initial `SaveRunState` + `SyncRunHistory` (:69-82).
- Completed-work detection on restart: status `completed` survives reconciliation only if `ValidateSourceReport`/`ValidateFinalReport` still pass (`run_state.go:312-350`); test pins rerun-after-artifact-deletion (`run_loop_test.go:257-278`). Failed tasks with future `RetryAfter` become `retrying`; expired ones go pending (:303-311).
- Resume across processes keeps session checkpoints: cancelled tasks retain `Session`; next invocation resumes with `SessionAction: "continue"` and falls back to fresh on incompatible fingerprint (`run.go:139-179`, `studySessionCompatible` :251-253). Pinned by `TestRunLoopPersistsAndContinuesCancelledStudySession` (`run_loop_test.go:132-181`).
- `--reset` flow: CLI confirm (`confirmRunLoopReplacement`) → `loadOrCreateRunLoopState` sees `req.Reset`, skips load, calls `archiveRunStateIfExists` (`run_loop.go:559-573`): renames `run-state.json` to `.ultraplan/archive/run-state-<UTC-timestamp>.json`, then builds fresh state. Only the state file is archived; ledger/history is preserved and keys prevent duplicate records (`recordHistory` dedup via `historyKeys`). Pinned by `TestRunLoopDefaultResumesExistingStateAndResetStartsFresh` (`run_loop_test.go:280-331`, asserts archive entries exist) and CLI `TestStudyRunLoopCommandConfirmsBeforeReplacingExistingState`.

## 6. Synthesize step

- Within `RunAll`: after each dimension-execution group's analyses complete, serially per dimension (`run_all.go:92-114`); skipped if no analyses ran (`hasAnalysisForDimension`) or blocked by `synthesisBlockers` (any non-completed sibling → `preflight_blocked` with blocker paths, :213-224). `Synthesize` itself re-runs preflight validation of every applicable source report and returns `preflight_blocked` before any runtime call (`synthesize.go:31-42`).
- Within `RunLoop`: synthesis tasks are graph nodes depending on their analyses; scheduler admits them once deps complete (`runnableTaskIDs` :613-631 checks `dependenciesCompleteFrom`); if dependencies reach terminal-but-not-complete states, `markSynthesisDependenciesFailed` fails the synthesis with code `synthesis.dependencies_failed` (:280-285, :857-865). Dimension order is "priority, but not a barrier" (:611-612 comment) so synthesis starts as soon as its own deps finish (`TestRunLoopSynthesizesDimensionAsSoonAsItsAnalysisCompletes`).
- Manual: `study synthesize <dim>` command (§1). Final report path: `FinalReportPath` (`reports.go:12`); publication deferred in loop mode (`DeferPublication: true`, `run_loop.go:316/:323`) and executed by a dedicated publication goroutine draining `publicationJobs` (:247-262) plus end-of-run `publishRunLoopState` publishing state+ledger+summary together (`publication.go:45-63`).

## 7. Cancellation / interruption

- Signals: `cmd/ultraplan/main.go:19` `signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)` → `deps.ctx` → `beginDurableCLICommand` derives the cancellable operation context (`durable_operations.go:130`); run-control's watchdog also cancels on `CancellationRequested` or lost heartbeat/snapshot errors (`controlOperation`, `durable_operations.go:223-264`).
- RunAll on cancel: producer stops dispatching, workers mark remaining tasks cancelled placeholders; synthesis emits `cancelled` results; `statusRunAll(result, ctx.Err() != nil)` → `cancelled` (`run_all.go:49`, :243-245).
- RunLoop on cancel: outer loop condition drains active workers then exits (`run_loop.go:344`); claimed-but-unstarted `runTask` marks its own task cancelled via `markTaskCancelled` (:264-270); in-flight tasks get `cancelled` category from runtime (`statusForRuntimeFailure`, `run.go:310-315`); unscheduled tasks stay `pending` (pinned by `TestRunLoopCancellationDoesNotCancelUnscheduledTasks`, which asserts zero history records too).
- Locking: `AcquireRunLoopLock` uses `O_EXCL` create, PID liveness check (`processAlive`, `locks.go:17-23`) with stale-lock removal-and-retry (:61-86), redacted command capture (`sanitizeCommand` :184-202); ownership-checked release refusing foreign locks (:116-118). `CancelRunLoop` SIGINTs the live owner cross-process (:141-159); `ForceUnlockRunLoop` removes the file (:161-167). Observation-side `RunLoopActive` treats missing/malformed/stale locks as inactive (:131-137).
- `cleanup_uncertain.go` role: server-shutdown path writes `cleanup-uncertain.json` *without* taking the lock ("the original owner may still hold that lock", :28-30); `ReconcileInterruptedRun` (:66-90) later takes the lock and converts orphaned active states into explicit `workflow.interrupted` cancellations (`reconcileInterruptedRunLocked` :100-150) — this is the serve/web shutdown complement; the CLI `RunLoop` instead relies on `ResumeValidateRunState` resetting actives to pending.

## 8. Failure isolation

- RunAll: a failing analysis becomes `failedAnalysisResult` and the pool continues (`run_all.go:75-78`); synthesis then reports blockers. No retries at this layer.
- RunLoop: runtime failures do **not** stop scheduling — they're folded into task state by `applyExecutionResult` (`run_loop.go:779-826`): retryable categories (`rate_limit, timeout, provider_unavailable, runtime_unavailable` → `executionShouldRetry` :841-848) set `TaskStatusRetrying` with `RetryAfter` (+10 min rate-limit, else +2 min, :850-855); others → `failed`. Scheduler waits via `waitUntilRetry` emitting retry-wait progress (:441-448, :481-501). What *does* stop new scheduling is `firstErr` — persistence/history/publication machinery errors (`stopScheduling`, :345-347) — while already-active workers drain. Sibling failure → synthesis marked failed only when deps are terminal-non-complete (`markSynthesisDependenciesFailed`), pinned by `TestRunLoopMarksSynthesisFailedWhenDependenciesTerminal`.

## 9. Observation

- `study status [--json]`: loads state, reconciles in memory only, attaches `LockInfoForStatus`, renders counts/Active/Failed sections (`study_commands.go:1112-1210`).
- Live progress: `renderRunLoopProgress` stdout lines with scope-vs-study counters; runtime events summarized with redaction (`runtimeProgressSummary` :429, `config.RedactValue("runtime."+key,…)`).
- Diagnostics: JSONL sampler at `diagnostics/run-loop-memory.jsonl` (5 s ticker, 8 MB rotate, phases `state.save.end`, `runtime.start/end`, `parallelism.throttled`, `disk.admission_paused`, child RSS/CPU per task); read back by `LoadRunLoopResourceHistory` (:422-454) and `SummarizeParallelismThrottle` (:401-420).
- History aggregation: append-only `tasks.jsonl` with idempotent key `RunID|TaskID|Attempts|CompletedAtRFC3339Nano` (`run_history.go:306-312`), crash-tolerant tail handling (:262-270 comment: "A crash or full disk can leave only the final JSONL record partial"); `runs summary` subcommand refreshes `summary.md` without runtime (`app/study_runs_commands.go:16-33`); `RenderRunHistorySummary` produces status/remaining/dimension/source/runtime/recent/slowest/failed tables (`run_history_summary.go:25-57`).

## 2. Publisher mechanics (`internal/platform/gitpublish/publisher.go`)

- Modes: `ModeOff`/`ModeCommit`/`ModeCommitAndPush` (:17-21). Off short-circuits `Result{Skipped: true}` with empty Repository (:69-71) — the sentinel that callers filter via `visiblePublication` (sprint/publication.go:123-128) and the `Repository == "" && Skipped` checks (study/publication.go:24, :59).

- Path selection — `publishPaths` (:169-198): `All` → `["."]`; otherwise clean→abs→`filepath.Rel(repo,…)` with escape rejection `"path %q escapes repository"`; deduped + sorted.
- Lock acquisition at `<git-common-dir>/ultraplan-publish.lock` (:100-116).
- Commit creation — `commitPaths` (:200-261):
  - Message required; identity appended as trailer: `message += "\n\nUltraPlan-Publication: " + identity` (:205-207).
  - Temporary index: `os.CreateTemp(common, "ultraplan-index-*")`, env `GIT_INDEX_FILE=…` (:213-224); sequence `read-tree <parent>` → `add -A -- <paths>` → `write-tree`.
  - No-op idempotency: if new tree == parent tree → return `(parent, false, nil)` (:237-243) — no empty commits on retry.
  - CAS branch update: `symbolic-ref -q HEAD` then `update-ref <ref> <commit> <parent>`; failure message "branch changed while committing" (:249-255).
  - Real-index reconcile: `reset -q HEAD -- <paths>`; if this fails the commit is still recorded (`committed=true`) plus error "reconcile index after commit" (:256-259).
  - Author identity is **not** overridden — `commit-tree` uses ambient git config user.name/email; `Identity` exists only as the message trailer.

  - Remote name validated by `validRemoteName` (:304-315) — rejects leading `-`, allows `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`.
  - Upstream resolution: `for-each-ref --format=%(upstream:remotename)/(upstream:remoteref) refs/heads/<branch>` (:140-152).
  - With upstream: `push --porcelain -- <upstreamRemote> HEAD:<upstreamRef>`; without: `push --porcelain --set-upstream -- <policy.Remote> HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` (:154-158). **No force flags anywhere.**
  - Bounded by `PushTimeout` context (default 2m, :62-64); deadline → "push timed out after %s" (:160-162).
- Environment hygiene: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `LC_ALL=C` layered over `os.Environ` (`gitEnvironment` :284-302); all output via `CombinedOutput`, errors embed the exact argv (:267-282).

- Planning: `<sprint>/flow-state.json` + stage artifact (:19-42); area-reasoning additionally publishes reasoning-template outputs resolved under `s.root` and aborts on manifest findings ("area-reasoning manifest is invalid", :20-35); code-context adds `.workspace.json` (:43-45).

- Review: `review.md` + `flow-state.json` (:84-89).
- Smoke: harness author-changed paths first (`prepared.HarnessRoot` + `AuthorChangedPaths`, :100-110), then workspace `smoke.md` + `flow-state.json`, plus `roadmap.md` only when `SmokePass && !DiagnosticOnly` (:111-118).

## 3. Locking

- Resource: an flock on the file `<git-common-dir>/ultraplan-publish.lock`, created `0o600` (publisher.go:112, lock_unix.go:18). The lock file itself is never deleted — exclusion comes solely from the kernel lock.
- `lock_unix.go` (linux‖darwin): `syscall.Flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` in a loop, retry every 100ms until ctx done (:22-39); `EWOULDBLOCK/EAGAIN` retried, other errors fatal; `release()` unlocks + closes (:42-48).
- `lock_other.go` (!linux && !darwin): **no mutual exclusion** — checks ctx once, opens/creates the file, returns (:14-23). A best-effort placeholder.
- Contention scope: per git common dir, so it serializes publishers across processes touching the same repository (e.g., concurrent CLI + web operations on one workspace repo). Stale handling is implicit: flock dies with the process; a leftover file never blocks.

## 4. Worktrees (`internal/sprint/execute_target.go`)

Record type `SprintWorkspace{SchemaVersion, SourceRoot, Path, Branch, Baseline, CreatedAt}` (:18-25) persisted at `<sprint>/.workspace.json` (`sprintWorkspacePath` :27), schema version pinned to 1 (:16).

**Resolution precedence — `resolveSprintTarget(sp, projectIndex, create)` (:56-82):**
1. `s.codeContextTarget` hook (test-only seam; set exclusively in code_context_test.go:123/:305, efficiency_improvements_test.go:66).
2. `ResolveExecuteTarget(s.root, projectIndex)` (:29-54): extracts `Target Implementation Directory` (regexes :229-238), resolves rel paths against workspace root, must exist and be a directory.
3. Try `loadSprintWorkspace` (:84-97; JSON decode + version/field checks). On success: `validateSprintWorkspace` → use `record.Path` (Source `.workspace.json`). Validation failure = fail-closed finding: "Restore the recorded worktree or explicitly recreate the sprint workspace." (:66-68). Unreadable/malformed record = separate finding (:71-73).
4. Missing record: `create=false` → direct source target (legacy compatibility); `create=true` → `createSprintWorkspace`.

**`validateSprintWorkspace(record, source)` (:99-123)** checks four things: `SourceRoot == current target`; `record.Path` exists and is a dir; `gitCommonDirectory(source) == gitCommonDirectory(record.Path)` ("worktree belongs to a different Git repository"); current branch of the worktree == recorded Branch. It does **not** compare `Baseline` against current HEAD and does not inspect worktree dirtiness.

**`createSprintWorkspace(sp, source, now)` (:136-181) full sequence:**
1. Source must be a Git toplevel and equal the declared target — "target must be the Git worktree root %q" (:137-144).
2. Clean-tree requirement: `status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal` must be empty — "target has uncommitted changes" (:145-151).
3. Baseline freeze: `rev-parse HEAD` captured before branching (:152-155).
4. Naming: branch `ultraplan/<safe(project)>/<safe(slug)>`; path sibling to source: `filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(root), "."+base(root)+"-ultraplan-worktrees", project, slug)` (:156-158). `safeGitComponent` lowercases, replaces `[^a-z0-9._-]+` with `-`, trims `.-`, fallback `"sprint"` (:192-200).
5. Pre-check `os.Lstat(path)` must not exist ("worktree path already exists", :159-161); `MkdirAll` parent 0755 (:162-164).
6. `git -C source worktree add -b <branch> <path> <baseline>` (:165-168) — new branch born at the frozen baseline.
7. Record written atomically via `atomicWriteFile` (temp + fsync + rename + dir sync, smoke.go:714-746).
8. Rollback on record-write failure only (:175-179): best-effort `git worktree remove <path>` (non-force) + `git branch -D <branch>`, then "persist sprint workspace". There is no rollback for failures between steps 5–6 beyond what git leaves.

- Path escape rejection in `publishPaths` (publisher.go:186-189); remote-name validation duplicated at config and publisher layers (both reject leading `-`, preventing option injection); explicit `--` separators in `add`/`push` argv.
- Credential-prompt suppression (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`) so pushes fail rather than hang.
- Detached-HEAD refusal; CAS `update-ref` guards concurrent branch movement; temp index isolates staging — user's pre-staged files survive (publisher_test.go:13-45 asserts `staged.txt` remains staged and commit contains only owned paths).
- No force-push, no `reset --hard`, no checkout/clean anywhere under `internal/platform/gitpublish`.
- Wrong-repo guard on reuse via common-dir equality (execute_target.go:110-117); wrong-repo guard on commit implicit in `rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the supplied root plus per-path containment relative to *that* repo.

- Transport adapters cannot choose publication paths — paths are computed inside product services (docs/architecture.md:177 claim matches code layout; web layer contains zero `gitpublish` references).

---

## 6. Failure / cancellation behavior

- **Commit fails mid-way:** objects may dangle; branch unchanged (CAS); error propagates after stage state was already persisted. Retry path: flow's `flowStageAlreadyValid` marks the stage complete → republish at flow.go:149; execute republishes when tasks remain resolved (execute.go:341). - **Push fails / times out:** local commit intact, command errors ("A failed push stops the command but leaves the stage complete and the local commit intact", docs/user-guide.md:307; docs/configuration.md:226). - **Study loop cancellation:** publication worker drains channel then `recordErr` surfaces first publish error (run_loop.go:250-262, 450-456); run state/history saved *before* `publishRunLoopState`, so durable state never depends on publication success.
- **Docs claims vs implementation:** recovery.md:68 states "Configured stage publication runs only after canonical validation and persistence" — matches gates in §1. recovery.md:86 "reconciliation required: `smoke.md` committed but flow state did not" — implementation commits both files in one `Publish` request (publication.go:111-114), so this divergence stems from the persistence step (saveSmokeAttempt vs artifact write ordering in smoke.go:31-38), not from partial git commits; automatic reconciliation is explicitly deferred there.

## 1. Trigger points & gating

- Defaults: `Git{StageCompletion: "off", Remote: "origin", PushTimeout: "2m"}` (config.go:190).
- Validation (config.Validate): modes limited to `"off", "commit", "commit-and-push"` (config.go:475-479); remote charset check (config.go:480-482, `validGitRemoteName` config.go:540); push timeout positive and ≤30m (config.go:483-486).
- Precedence: `Load()` = Defaults → workspace `ultraplan.yml` (loadFile, config.go:159-163) → env overrides `ULTRAPLAN_GIT_STAGE_COMPLETION` / `ULTRAPLAN_GIT_REMOTE` / `ULTRAPLAN_GIT_PUSH_TIMEOUT` (config.go:137-139) → CLI (only logging fields, config.go:167+; no git CLI override). Sources map tags each field `default|workspace|env`.

### Composition root (`internal/app/git_publication.go`)

## 2. Publisher mechanics (`internal/platform/gitpublish/publisher.go`)

- Modes: `ModeOff`/`ModeCommit`/`ModeCommitAndPush` (:17-21). Off short-circuits `Result{Skipped: true}` with empty Repository (:69-71) — the sentinel that callers filter via `visiblePublication` (sprint/publication.go:123-128) and the `Repository == "" && Skipped` checks (study/publication.go:24, :59).
- Repo resolution: `rev-parse --show-toplevel` from `req.Root` (:79-86) — Root may be a subdir; commit lands in the containing repo. Branch from `branch --show-current`; detached HEAD rejected: "detached HEAD is not supported" (:87-94).
- Path selection — `publishPaths` (:169-198): `All` → `["."]`; otherwise clean→abs→`filepath.Rel(repo,…)` with escape rejection `"path %q escapes repository"`; deduped + sorted.
- Lock acquisition at `<git-common-dir>/ultraplan-publish.lock` (:100-116).
- Commit creation — `commitPaths` (:200-261):
  - Message required; identity appended as trailer: `message += "\n\nUltraPlan-Publication: " + identity` (:205-207).
  - Temporary index: `os.CreateTemp(common, "ultraplan-index-*")`, env `GIT_INDEX_FILE=…` (:213-224); sequence `read-tree <parent>` → `add -A -- <paths>` → `write-tree`.
  - No-op idempotency: if new tree == parent tree → return `(parent, false, nil)` (:237-243) — no empty commits on retry.
  - CAS branch update: `symbolic-ref -q HEAD` then `update-ref <ref> <commit> <parent>`; failure message "branch changed while committing" (:249-255).
  - Real-index reconcile: `reset -q HEAD -- <paths>`; if this fails the commit is still recorded (`committed=true`) plus error "reconcile index after commit" (:256-259).
  - Author identity is **not** overridden — `commit-tree` uses ambient git config user.name/email; `Identity` exists only as the message trailer.
- Push (:132-166), only in `ModeCommitAndPush`:
  - Remote name validated by `validRemoteName` (:304-315) — rejects leading `-`, allows `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`.
  - Upstream resolution: `for-each-ref --format=%(upstream:remotename)/(upstream:remoteref) refs/heads/<branch>` (:140-152).
  - With upstream: `push --porcelain -- <upstreamRemote> HEAD:<upstreamRef>`; without: `push --porcelain --set-upstream -- <policy.Remote> HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` (:154-158). **No force flags anywhere.**
  - Bounded by `PushTimeout` context (default 2m, :62-64); deadline → "push timed out after %s" (:160-162).
- Environment hygiene: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `LC_ALL=C` layered over `os.Environ` (`gitEnvironment` :284-302); all output via `CombinedOutput`, errors embed the exact argv (:267-282).

**What exactly gets committed per stage** (from `internal/sprint/publication.go`, `internal/study/publication.go`):
- Planning: `<sprint>/flow-state.json` + stage artifact (:19-42); area-reasoning additionally publishes reasoning-template outputs resolved under `s.root` and aborts on manifest findings ("area-reasoning manifest is invalid", :20-35); code-context adds `.workspace.json` (:43-45).
- Execute: two publishes — target repo with `All: true` (:63) then workspace repo with `execute.md` + `.run-state.json` (:68-75). Identities suffixed `/implementation` and `/workspace`. Test pin: publication_test.go:55-74 ("TestPublishExecuteUsesTargetBeforeWorkspace").
- Review: `review.md` + `flow-state.json` (:84-89).
- Smoke: harness author-changed paths first (`prepared.HarnessRoot` + `AuthorChangedPaths`, :100-110), then workspace `smoke.md` + `flow-state.json`, plus `roadmap.md` only when `SmokePass && !DiagnosticOnly` (:111-118).
- Study execution: report `OutputPath` + extras (:14); run-all summary path (:35); run-loop state triple `RunStatePath/RunHistoryPath/RunHistorySummaryPath` (:49-58; defined run_state.go:188-190, run_history.go:68-74).
- Message formats: sprint `"ultraplan: sprint %s/%s complete %s"`, study execution `"ultraplan: study %s complete %s %s"`, run-all `"…complete run-all"`, run-state `"…update run state"`.

---

## 3. Locking

- Resource: an flock on the file `<git-common-dir>/ultraplan-publish.lock`, created `0o600` (publisher.go:112, lock_unix.go:18). The lock file itself is never deleted — exclusion comes solely from the kernel lock.
- `lock_unix.go` (linux‖darwin): `syscall.Flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` in a loop, retry every 100ms until ctx done (:22-39); `EWOULDBLOCK/EAGAIN` retried, other errors fatal; `release()` unlocks + closes (:42-48).
- `lock_other.go` (!linux && !darwin): **no mutual exclusion** — checks ctx once, opens/creates the file, returns (:14-23). A best-effort placeholder.
- Contention scope: per git common dir, so it serializes publishers across processes touching the same repository (e.g., concurrent CLI + web operations on one workspace repo). Stale handling is implicit: flock dies with the process; a leftover file never blocks.

---

## 4. Worktrees (`internal/sprint/execute_target.go`)

Record type `SprintWorkspace{SchemaVersion, SourceRoot, Path, Branch, Baseline, CreatedAt}` (:18-25) persisted at `<sprint>/.workspace.json` (`sprintWorkspacePath` :27), schema version pinned to 1 (:16).

**Resolution precedence — `resolveSprintTarget(sp, projectIndex, create)` (:56-82):**
1. `s.codeContextTarget` hook (test-only seam; set exclusively in code_context_test.go:123/:305, efficiency_improvements_test.go:66).
2. `ResolveExecuteTarget(s.root, projectIndex)` (:29-54): extracts `Target Implementation Directory` (regexes :229-238), resolves rel paths against workspace root, must exist and be a directory.
3. Try `loadSprintWorkspace` (:84-97; JSON decode + version/field checks). On success: `validateSprintWorkspace` → use `record.Path` (Source `.workspace.json`). Validation failure = fail-closed finding: "Restore the recorded worktree or explicitly recreate the sprint workspace." (:66-68). Unreadable/malformed record = separate finding (:71-73).
4. Missing record: `create=false` → direct source target (legacy compatibility); `create=true` → `createSprintWorkspace`.

**`validateSprintWorkspace(record, source)` (:99-123)** checks four things: `SourceRoot == current target`; `record.Path` exists and is a dir; `gitCommonDirectory(source) == gitCommonDirectory(record.Path)` ("worktree belongs to a different Git repository"); current branch of the worktree == recorded Branch. It does **not** compare `Baseline` against current HEAD and does not inspect worktree dirtiness.

**`createSprintWorkspace(sp, source, now)` (:136-181) full sequence:**
1. Source must be a Git toplevel and equal the declared target — "target must be the Git worktree root %q" (:137-144).
2. Clean-tree requirement: `status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal` must be empty — "target has uncommitted changes" (:145-151).
3. Baseline freeze: `rev-parse HEAD` captured before branching (:152-155).
4. Naming: branch `ultraplan/<safe(project)>/<safe(slug)>`; path sibling to source: `filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(root), "."+base(root)+"-ultraplan-worktrees", project, slug)` (:156-158). `safeGitComponent` lowercases, replaces `[^a-z0-9._-]+` with `-`, trims `.-`, fallback `"sprint"` (:192-200).
5. Pre-check `os.Lstat(path)` must not exist ("worktree path already exists", :159-161); `MkdirAll` parent 0755 (:162-164).
6. `git -C source worktree add -b <branch> <path> <baseline>` (:165-168) — new branch born at the frozen baseline.
7. Record written atomically via `atomicWriteFile` (temp + fsync + rename + dir sync, smoke.go:714-746).
8. Rollback on record-write failure only (:175-179): best-effort `git worktree remove <path>` (non-force) + `git branch -D <branch>`, then "persist sprint workspace". There is no rollback for failures between steps 5–6 beyond what git leaves.

**Reuse conditions:** any later `resolveSprintTarget` loads the record and validates; a dirty worktree is acceptable (pinned by sprint_workspace_test.go:34-40). Creation triggers: flow.go:138 and code_context.go:270 only; all other consumers pass `create=false` (execute.go:360 prepareExecute, review.go:212, smoke_protocol.go:126, prompt_context.go:106, code_context.go:214 PromptCodeContext, service.go:510).

**Cleanup/prune:** absent from production code. The only `worktree remove` outside creation-rollback is test-fixture cleanup (sprint_workspace_test.go:101-113). Docs agree: "UltraPlan will not rebase, retarget, remove, or recreate it automatically." (docs/user-guide.md:303)

**Runtime binding:** execute runtime runs with `runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path` (execute.go:245, code_context.go:306). Note: `ValidateExecuteWorkdir` (:202-218, containment "escapes approved target") has no production caller found — only its definition and its test (execute_target_test.go:52-66); enforcement at runtime is via prompt-level `ExecuteSafetyInstructions` (:220-227, e.g., "Do not run or request Git mutation…") embedded into the execute prompt (execute.go:472) and the skills text (workspace/skills.go:391).

---

## 5. Safety controls observed

- Path escape rejection in `publishPaths` (publisher.go:186-189); remote-name validation duplicated at config and publisher layers (both reject leading `-`, preventing option injection); explicit `--` separators in `add`/`push` argv.
- Credential-prompt suppression (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`) so pushes fail rather than hang.
- Detached-HEAD refusal; CAS `update-ref` guards concurrent branch movement; temp index isolates staging — user's pre-staged files survive (publisher_test.go:13-45 asserts `staged.txt` remains staged and commit contains only owned paths).
- No force-push, no `reset --hard`, no checkout/clean anywhere under `internal/platform/gitpublish`.
- Wrong-repo guard on reuse via common-dir equality (execute_target.go:110-117); wrong-repo guard on commit implicit in `rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the supplied root plus per-path containment relative to *that* repo.
- Publication gates: dry runs never publish; cancelled/failed stages never publish (`Status != ExecutionStatusCompleted` skip, study/publication.go:11; review blocked verdict exits at persistReviewFailure before publish, review.go:604-607); smoke DiagnosticOnly skips roadmap append and whole publication unless `SmokeCompleted` (smoke.go:49).
- Transport adapters cannot choose publication paths — paths are computed inside product services (docs/architecture.md:177 claim matches code layout; web layer contains zero `gitpublish` references).

---

## 6. Failure / cancellation behavior

- **Commit fails mid-way:** objects may dangle; branch unchanged (CAS); error propagates after stage state was already persisted. Retry path: flow's `flowStageAlreadyValid` marks the stage complete → republish at flow.go:149; execute republishes when tasks remain resolved (execute.go:341). Tree-equality no-op makes re-commit harmless.
- **Push fails / times out:** local commit intact, command errors ("A failed push stops the command but leaves the stage complete and the local commit intact", docs/user-guide.md:307; docs/configuration.md:226). Pinned by `TestPublisherRetriesPushWithoutDuplicateCommit` (publisher_test.go:47-80): retry yields `Committed=false, Pushed=true, same SHA`.
- **Reset-reconcile failure:** commit kept, `committed=true` + error (publisher.go:256-259).
- **Process death during publish:** flock auto-released; `defer os.Remove(indexPath)` does not run on SIGKILL, so `ultraplan-index-*` temp files can linger in the git common dir (mechanism observation, publisher.go:213-223).
- **Study loop cancellation:** publication worker drains channel then `recordErr` surfaces first publish error (run_loop.go:250-262, 450-456); run state/history saved *before* `publishRunLoopState`, so durable state never depends on publication success.
- **Docs claims vs implementation:** recovery.md:68 states "Configured stage publication runs only after canonical validation and persistence" — matches gates in §1. recovery.md:86 "reconciliation required: `smoke.md` committed but flow state did not" — implementation commits both files in one `Publish` request (publication.go:111-114), so this divergence stems from the persistence step (saveSmokeAttempt vs artifact write ordering in smoke.go:31-38), not from partial git commits; automatic reconciliation is explicitly deferred there.

---

## 7. Pinning tests

| File | Pins |
|---|---|
| gitpublish/publisher_test.go:13-45 | Owned-paths-only commit; user's unrelated staged index preserved; `UltraPlan-Publication:` trailer present |
| gitpublish/publisher_test.go:47-80 | Push retry without duplicate commit; upstream set on bare remote; same commit SHA pushed |
| sprint/publication_test.go:26-53 | Planning publish uses exactly `{requirements.md, flow-state.json}`, `Root=root`, `All=false` |
| sprint/publication_test.go:55-74 | Execute order: target-first with `All:true`, then workspace paths |
| study/publication_test.go:19-40 | Publish request carries OutputPath + extra path; identity format `study/demo/analysis/02-runtime/source` |
| study/publication_test.go:42-51 | Failed/validation-failed stage never published |
| sprint/sprint_workspace_test.go:13-41 | Baseline frozen (`worktree HEAD == record.Baseline`), branch naming, dirty-worktree reuse |
| sprint/sprint_workspace_test.go:43-57 | Dirty source rejected; no `.workspace.json` left behind |
| sprint/sprint_workspace_test.go:59-85 | Completed code-context materializes workspace without rerunning the stage |
| sprint/execute_target_test.go | Target resolution (abs/relative/missing/unavailable), `ValidateExecuteWorkdir` containment, safety-instruction content |
| platform/config/config_test.go:157-189 | Git defaults; env-beats-workspace precedence (`ULTRAPLAN_GIT_STAGE_COMPLETION`); invalid mode/remote/timeout rejected |

Gap note (factual, not a finding): no unit test references `stagePublisher` or constructs `gitpublish` policies inside `internal/app` tests; the app-layer wiring is covered only indirectly via config tests.

---

## 8. Seams & config precedence recap

- **Primary seam:** `gitpublish.Publisher` interface (publisher.go:47-49). Services receive it via `sprint.Service.WithPublisher` (service.go:42, :60-63) and `study.WithPublisher` option (study/service.go:14, :100-104); nil disables everything (each publish fn begins `if s.publisher == nil { return … }`).
- **Translation seam:** app-layer `stagePublisher` maps validated config → `Policy` once at composition; three sprint construction sites and three study sites (§1).
- **Clock seam:** `WithClock` feeds `CreatedAt` (service.go:48; used in sprint_workspace_test.go:18).
- **Target seam:** `codeContextTarget` func field, test-only (grep confirms no production setter).
- **Publication points across loops:** flow (per-stage ×2 paths + FlowStage), execute (terminal, all-resolved), review (post-state-save), smoke (post-terminal + roadmap condition), study run/synthesize (inline, skippable via `DeferPublication`), study run-loop (serialized worker + terminal run-state), run-all (summary tail).
- **Config precedence:** defaults → `ultraplan.yml` → `ULTRAPLAN_GIT_*` env → (CLI touches nothing git-related), all recorded in `Effective.Sources` (config.go:153-166, :275-288).

### Uncertainty notes
- `ValidateExecuteWorkdir` appears production-unused based on exhaustive grep (definition + tests only); I did not audit `cmd/` cobra-style wiring beyond `internal/app` since all command dispatch flows through `internal/app` handlers grepped here.
- Non-unix `lock_other.go` behavior under Windows git (which does support some locking) is untested in-repo; CI targets unknown.
- Exact git-version dependence of `%(upstream:remotename)`/`--porcelain` push output parsing was not verified against a git compatibility matrix.
